purpose: Lints a caller-declared token-record schema against the published PCI DSS v4.0.1 account-data rules and reports which declared surfaces expose more account data than the rule allows. The input is a synthetic record schema: typed fields (primary account number, card verification code, PIN or PIN block, full track data, deterministic digest, other) each carrying a mask expression string, an optional alias template, declared search-index expressions, and a list of stored data elements each with a sensitive-authentication-data class, a retention state, a storage location class and an encryption flag. Checks: per-field display exposure against the first-six-and-last-four digit masking ceiling (Requirement 3.4.1), the same ceiling over the alias template and each declared search-index expression, retention of sensitive authentication data after authorization including encrypted storage (Requirements 3.3.1, 3.3.1.1, 3.3.1.2, 3.3.1.3), and digest fields presented as rendering the PAN unreadable, for a fragment digest target or an unkeyed hash (Requirements 3.5.1, 3.5.1.1). Carve-outs the caller owns the facts for (non-persistent short-term retention conditions, digest-and-truncation correlation controls) resolve to named manual-review flags, never to a clean pass; unrecognized input values refuse the whole call with INPUT_REFUSED rather than guessing. Scope limits: the node sees only what the caller declares; it expresses no opinion on business-need role lists, issuer carve-outs, deletion processes, key management, or display surfaces it was not told about; and it checks a schema declaration, not a production data store, so a verdict is not a PCI DSS assessment. Findings arrive as Policy Mandate-ready flags with a mirrored issues list; deterministic, zero network, zero PII.
